newsitem.title: UK: Gulf Canada lifts Clyde bid to 120p/shr.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Canada lifts Clyde bid to 120p/shr.

text.p: Gulf Canada Resources stepped up its battle to gain control of Britain's Clyde Petroleum Plc on Tuesday, raising its bid to 120 pence per share from 105 pence per share.

The new offer is below the 125 pence level some analysts had been looking for. Gulf Canada said in a statement that the new bid valued Clyde at 494.6 million pounds ($793 million), up from 432 million pounds.
Gulf Canada lifts Clyde bid to 120p/shr

Gulf said the bid represented a 42 percent premium to Clyde's share price on December 17, the day before its first offer was announced. J.P. Bryan, president and chief executive officer of Gulf Canada, said the offer "provides cash now for a company with little or no upside due to its lack of exploration success and potential."
In the increasingly bitter war of words between the two companies, Bryan accused Clyde of having low reserves, failing to replace production and being over dependent on acquisitions."
Clyde has previously accused Gulf Canada of undervaluing it in terms of its cash flow multiple, a favoured method for valuing oil companies in North America.
Soem analysts believe a rival bid for Clyde could now emerge, and Gulf Canada said on Tuesday that it reserved the right to raise its offer further if a competitor came forward. ($1=.6237 Pound)
